A FileSet resource says what a backup job saves: the Include blocks list files and plugins with Options blocks for compression, signatures and patterns; Exclude blocks leave things out.

## Examples

**Linux system with excludes**

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Include {
    Options {
      Signature = XXH128
      Compression = LZ4
      One FS = no
      FS Type = ext4, xfs, btrfs
    }
    Options {
      Wild Dir = "*/.cache"
      Wild File = "*.tmp"
      Exclude = yes
    }
    File = /
    Exclude Dir Containing = .nobackup
  }
  Exclude {
    File = /var/lib/bareos
    File = /proc
    File = /tmp
  }
}
```

The first Options block whose patterns match decides: .cache directories and \*.tmp files are excluded, everything else on ext4, xfs and btrfs file systems is saved with checksum and compression.

**A database through a plugin**

```text
FileSet {
  Name = PostgreSQL
  Include {
    Options {
      Signature = XXH128
    }
    Plugin = "python3:module_name=bareos-fd-postgresql"
  }
}
```

## Directives

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Name](#d-name) | name |  | required | Name of the FileSet. |

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name · Required

Name of the FileSet.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = "LinuxAll"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add fileset name=LinuxAll
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the FileSet.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Description = "All local file systems"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update fileset=LinuxAll description="All local file systems"
```

### Include {#d-include}

Key: `include` · Type: block

Block with the files to back up (File, Plugin) and Options blocks that say how. A FileSet may have several Include blocks. See the Include block.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Include {
    Options {
      Signature = XXH128
    }
    File = /etc
    File = /home
  }
}
```

### Exclude {#d-exclude}

Key: `exclude` · Type: block

Block with files and directories to leave out (File lines). Patterns go into an Options block with Exclude = yes instead.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Exclude {
    File = /home/*/.cache
    File = /tmp
  }
}
```

### Ignore File Set Changes {#d-ignorefilesetchanges}

Key: `ignorefilesetchanges` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Normally a change of the FileSet makes the next Incremental or Differential a Full, since the old backups do not contain the new files. With yes the change is ignored; new files then only appear in the next Full.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Ignore File Set Changes = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update fileset=LinuxAll ignorefilesetchanges=yes
```

### Enable VSS {#d-enablevss}

Key: `enablevss` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

On Windows clients: back up from a Volume Shadow Copy snapshot, so open files are consistent.

```text
FileSet {
  Name = LinuxAll
  Enable VSS = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update fileset=LinuxAll enablevss=yes
```

## Include block {#block-include}

Files and plugins to back up, with Options blocks.

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [File](#b-include-file) | path |  |  | A file or directory to back up; directories are backed up recursively. |
| [Plugin](#b-include-plugin) | string |  |  | A File Daemon plugin with its options that delivers the data instead of files, for example a database plugin. |
| [Exclude Dir Containing](#b-include-excludedircontaining) | string |  |  | Leave out every directory that contains a file of this name, so users can mark directories with a .nobackup file. |
| [Options](#b-include-options) | block |  |  | Block of options for the files of this Include. |

### File {#b-include-file}

Key: `file` · Type: path

A file or directory to back up; directories are backed up recursively. Repeat it for several paths. "|command" uses the output of a command on the Director as list, "\\\\|command" one run on the client, and "&lt;file" ("\\\\&lt;file" on the client) reads the list from a file.

```text
File = /home
```

### Plugin {#b-include-plugin}

Key: `plugin` · Type: string

A File Daemon plugin with its options that delivers the data instead of files, for example a database plugin. The Onesimus Director masks secrets in plugin lines in show output and in the FileSet text stored in the catalog; the File Daemon still gets the real line.

```text
Plugin = "python3:module_name=bareos-fd-postgresql:db_host=localhost"
```

### Exclude Dir Containing {#b-include-excludedircontaining}

Key: `excludedircontaining` · Type: string

Leave out every directory that contains a file of this name, so users can mark directories with a .nobackup file.

```text
Exclude Dir Containing = .nobackup
```

### Options {#b-include-options}

Key: `options` · Type: block

Block of options for the files of this Include. Several Options blocks may be given: the first block whose patterns match a file decides; a block without patterns applies to all remaining files. See the Options block.

```text
Options {
  Signature = XXH128
  Compression = LZ4
}
```

## Exclude block {#block-exclude}

Files and directories to leave out.

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [File](#b-exclude-file) | path |  |  | A file or directory that is left out. |

### File {#b-exclude-file}

Key: `file` · Type: path

A file or directory that is left out. Wildcards are not interpreted here; use an Options block with Wild and Exclude = yes for patterns.

```text
File = /var/tmp
```

## Options block {#block-options}

Options of an Include block. Several blocks may be given; the first block whose patterns (Wild, Regex, ...) match a file decides, a block without patterns applies to all other files. The option keywords and values follow the Onesimus Director's port of the C++ table (inc\_conf.cc); Hard Links defaults to no, Acl Support and Xattr Support to yes.

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Signature](#b-options-signature) | enum |  |  | Checksum stored for every file, used by verify jobs and Accurate mode to detect changes. |
| [Compression](#b-options-compression) | enum |  |  | Software compression on the client. |
| [Encryption](#b-options-encryption) | enum |  |  | Cipher for data encryption on the client. |
| [Force Encryption](#b-options-forceencryption) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Fail the job instead of backing up unencrypted when encryption is not possible. |
| [One FS](#b-options-onefs) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Stay on the file system of each File line and do not descend into other mounted file systems. |
| [Recurse](#b-options-recurse) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Back up directories recursively. |
| [Sparse](#b-options-sparse) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Store sparse files efficiently (holes are not stored), for example virtual machine images. |
| [Hard Links](#b-options-hardlinks) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Detect hard links and store the data of a multiply linked file once. |
| [Replace](#b-options-replace) | enum | `always` |  | Default replace mode for restores of these files. |
| [Read Fifo](#b-options-readfifo) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Read the data from named pipes (FIFOs) instead of saving them as special files, for example to back up a database dump written into a pipe by a Client Run Before Job script. |
| [Portable](#b-options-portable) | yes\|no | `no` |  | On Windows: store files in a portable format (without Windows backup streams), so they can be restored on other systems, at the cost of security information. |
| [Mtime Only](#b-options-mtimeonly) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Select files for Incremental and Differential backups by modification time only, ignoring the change time (ctime). |
| [Keep Atime](#b-options-keepatime) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Reset the access time of each file after reading it. |
| [Noatime](#b-options-noatime) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Open files with O\_NOATIME so reading does not change the access time (Linux, file owner or root). |
| [Exclude](#b-options-exclude) | yes\|no | `no` |  | The files matched by the patterns of this Options block are excluded instead of included. |
| [Acl Support](#b-options-aclsupport) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Back up POSIX and NFSv4 ACLs. |
| [Xattr Support](#b-options-xattrsupport) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Back up extended attributes (for example SELinux labels). |
| [Ignore Case](#b-options-ignorecase) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Match Wild and Regex patterns without regard to case; useful for Windows clients. |
| [Hfs Plus Support](#b-options-hfsplussupport) | yes\|no | `no` |  | On macOS: back up HFS+ resource forks and Finder information. |
| [Enhanced Wild](#b-options-enhancedwild) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Accepted for compatibility; the Director stores it like Noatime (the C++ Director does the same). |
| [Check File Changes](#b-options-checkfilechanges) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Check after reading a file whether it changed while it was saved, and warn if so. |
| [Honor No Dump Flag](#b-options-honornodumpflag) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Skip files that carry the nodump flag (chattr +d). |
| [Shadowing](#b-options-shadowing) | enum | `none` |  | Detects File lines that lie inside other File lines (and would be saved twice): warn about them or remove them, within this Include (local) or the whole FileSet (global). |
| [Auto Exclude](#b-options-autoexclude) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | On Windows: honour the files the system lists as not to be backed up (FilesNotToBackup). |
| [Verify](#b-options-verify) | string |  |  | Attributes compared by verify jobs, as option letters: i inode, p permissions, n links, u user, g group, s size, a atime, m mtime, c ctime, d size decrease, 5 MD5, 1 SHA1. |
| [Accurate](#b-options-accurate) | string |  |  | Attributes compared in Accurate mode to decide whether a file changed, as option letters like Verify (default mcs: mtime, ctime and size). |
| [Strip Path](#b-options-strippath) | positive integer |  |  | Removes this many leading path components before the files are stored. |
| [Size](#b-options-size) | string |  |  | Select files by size: a size, a range (10k-1m) or a comparison (&lt;1m, &gt;1g). |
| [Wild](#b-options-wild) | pattern |  |  | Shell wildcard (\* ? \[ \]) matched against the full path; repeatable. |
| [Wild Dir](#b-options-wilddir) | pattern |  |  | Wildcard matched against directory paths only. |
| [Wild File](#b-options-wildfile) | pattern |  |  | Wildcard matched against file names (not directories); a pattern without / matches the base name. |
| [Regex](#b-options-regex) | pattern |  |  | POSIX extended regular expression matched against the full path; repeatable. |
| [Regex Dir](#b-options-regexdir) | pattern |  |  | Regular expression matched against directory paths only. |
| [Regex File](#b-options-regexfile) | pattern |  |  | Regular expression matched against file paths only. |
| [FS Type](#b-options-fstype) | string list |  |  | Only back up file systems of these types (ext4, xfs, btrfs, ...). |
| [Drive Type](#b-options-drivetype) | string list |  |  | On Windows: only back up drives of these types (fixed, removable, remote, cdrom, ramdisk). |
| [Meta](#b-options-meta) | string list |  |  | Meta information passed to plugins. |
| [Plugin](#b-options-plugin) | string |  |  | Plugin that handles the files of this Options block. |

### Signature {#b-options-signature}

Key: `signature` · Type: enum · Values: `MD5`, `SHA1`, `SHA256`, `SHA512`, `XXH128`

Checksum stored for every file, used by verify jobs and Accurate mode to detect changes. XXH128 is fast; SHA256 or SHA512 are cryptographic. Without it no checksum is stored.

```text
Signature = XXH128
```

### Compression {#b-options-compression}

Key: `compression` · Type: enum · Values: `GZIP`, `GZIP1`, `GZIP2`, `GZIP3`, `GZIP4`, `GZIP5`, `GZIP6`, `GZIP7`, `GZIP8`, `GZIP9`, `LZO`, `LZFAST`, `LZ4`, `LZ4HC`

Software compression on the client. LZ4 is fast with moderate gain, GZIP6 (= GZIP) compresses better but costs CPU. Leave it off for data that is compressed already and for tape drives that compress in hardware (see Allow Compression of the Storage).

```text
Compression = LZ4
```

### Encryption {#b-options-encryption}

Key: `encryption` · Type: enum · Values: `blowfish`, `3des`, `aes128`, `aes192`, `aes256`, `camellia128`, `camellia192`, `camellia256`, `aes128hmacsha1`, `aes256hmacsha1`

Cipher for data encryption on the client. Encryption also needs PKI keys in the File Daemon's configuration; without the private key the data cannot be restored.

```text
Encryption = aes256
```

### Force Encryption {#b-options-forceencryption}

Key: `forceencryption` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Fail the job instead of backing up unencrypted when encryption is not possible.

```text
Force Encryption = yes
```

### One FS {#b-options-onefs}

Key: `onefs` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Stay on the file system of each File line and do not descend into other mounted file systems. With no, mount points are crossed; then FS Type helps to skip /proc, /sys and network file systems.

```text
One FS = no
```

### Recurse {#b-options-recurse}

Key: `recurse` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Back up directories recursively. With no, only the entries directly in a listed directory are saved.

```text
Recurse = no
```

### Sparse {#b-options-sparse}

Key: `sparse` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Store sparse files efficiently (holes are not stored), for example virtual machine images.

```text
Sparse = yes
```

### Hard Links {#b-options-hardlinks}

Key: `hardlinks` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Detect hard links and store the data of a multiply linked file once. In Bareos 25 the default is no (each link is saved as a file), which saves memory on clients with many files; the Onesimus Director has the same default.

```text
Hard Links = yes
```

### Replace {#b-options-replace}

Key: `replace` · Type: enum · Default: `always` · Values: `always`, `ifnewer`, `never`

Default replace mode for restores of these files.

```text
Replace = ifnewer
```

### Read Fifo {#b-options-readfifo}

Key: `readfifo` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Read the data from named pipes (FIFOs) instead of saving them as special files, for example to back up a database dump written into a pipe by a Client Run Before Job script.

```text
Read Fifo = yes
```

### Portable {#b-options-portable}

Key: `portable` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

On Windows: store files in a portable format (without Windows backup streams), so they can be restored on other systems, at the cost of security information.

```text
Portable = yes
```

### Mtime Only {#b-options-mtimeonly}

Key: `mtimeonly` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Select files for Incremental and Differential backups by modification time only, ignoring the change time (ctime).

```text
Mtime Only = yes
```

### Keep Atime {#b-options-keepatime}

Key: `keepatime` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Reset the access time of each file after reading it. This changes the ctime, so Incrementals would save the files again unless Mtime Only is set; Noatime is usually the better choice.

```text
Keep Atime = yes
```

### Noatime {#b-options-noatime}

Key: `noatime` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Open files with O\_NOATIME so reading does not change the access time (Linux, file owner or root).

```text
Noatime = yes
```

### Exclude {#b-options-exclude}

Key: `exclude` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

The files matched by the patterns of this Options block are excluded instead of included.

```text
Exclude = yes
```

### Acl Support {#b-options-aclsupport}

Key: `aclsupport` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Back up POSIX and NFSv4 ACLs. Default yes in Bareos 25 and in the Onesimus Director.

```text
Acl Support = no
```

### Xattr Support {#b-options-xattrsupport}

Key: `xattrsupport` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Back up extended attributes (for example SELinux labels). Default yes in Bareos 25.

```text
Xattr Support = no
```

### Ignore Case {#b-options-ignorecase}

Key: `ignorecase` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Match Wild and Regex patterns without regard to case; useful for Windows clients.

```text
Ignore Case = yes
```

### Hfs Plus Support {#b-options-hfsplussupport}

Key: `hfsplussupport` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

On macOS: back up HFS+ resource forks and Finder information.

```text
Hfs Plus Support = yes
```

### Enhanced Wild {#b-options-enhancedwild}

Key: `enhancedwild` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Accepted for compatibility; the Director stores it like Noatime (the C++ Director does the same).

```text
Enhanced Wild = no
```

### Check File Changes {#b-options-checkfilechanges}

Key: `checkfilechanges` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Check after reading a file whether it changed while it was saved, and warn if so.

```text
Check File Changes = yes
```

### Honor No Dump Flag {#b-options-honornodumpflag}

Key: `honornodumpflag` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Skip files that carry the nodump flag (chattr +d).

```text
Honor No Dump Flag = yes
```

### Shadowing {#b-options-shadowing}

Key: `shadowing` · Type: enum · Default: `none` · Values: `none`, `localwarn`, `localremove`, `globalwarn`, `globalremove`

Detects File lines that lie inside other File lines (and would be saved twice): warn about them or remove them, within this Include (local) or the whole FileSet (global).

```text
Shadowing = localremove
```

### Auto Exclude {#b-options-autoexclude}

Key: `autoexclude` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

On Windows: honour the files the system lists as not to be backed up (FilesNotToBackup).

```text
Auto Exclude = no
```

### Verify {#b-options-verify}

Key: `verify` · Type: string

Attributes compared by verify jobs, as option letters: i inode, p permissions, n links, u user, g group, s size, a atime, m mtime, c ctime, d size decrease, 5 MD5, 1 SHA1.

```text
Verify = pins5
```

### Accurate {#b-options-accurate}

Key: `accurate` · Type: string

Attributes compared in Accurate mode to decide whether a file changed, as option letters like Verify (default mcs: mtime, ctime and size).

```text
Accurate = mcs
```

### Strip Path {#b-options-strippath}

Key: `strippath` · Type: positive integer

Removes this many leading path components before the files are stored.

```text
Strip Path = 1
```

### Size {#b-options-size}

Key: `size` · Type: string

Select files by size: a size, a range (10k-1m) or a comparison (&lt;1m, &gt;1g).

```text
Size = >1g
```

### Wild {#b-options-wild}

Key: `wild` · Type: pattern

Shell wildcard (\* ? \[ \]) matched against the full path; repeatable. Files that match are handled by this Options block (included, or excluded with Exclude = yes).

```text
Wild = "*.iso"
```

### Wild Dir {#b-options-wilddir}

Key: `wilddir` · Type: pattern

Wildcard matched against directory paths only.

```text
Wild Dir = "*/.cache"
```

### Wild File {#b-options-wildfile}

Key: `wildfile` · Type: pattern

Wildcard matched against file names (not directories); a pattern without / matches the base name.

```text
Wild File = "*.tmp"
```

### Regex {#b-options-regex}

Key: `regex` · Type: pattern

POSIX extended regular expression matched against the full path; repeatable.

```text
Regex = "\\.(mp4|mkv)$"
```

### Regex Dir {#b-options-regexdir}

Key: `regexdir` · Type: pattern

Regular expression matched against directory paths only.

```text
Regex Dir = "/node_modules$"
```

### Regex File {#b-options-regexfile}

Key: `regexfile` · Type: pattern

Regular expression matched against file paths only.

```text
Regex File = "\\.o$"
```

### FS Type {#b-options-fstype}

Key: `fstype` · Type: string list

Only back up file systems of these types (ext4, xfs, btrfs, ...). Together with One FS = no it selects the local file systems and skips proc, sysfs, tmpfs and network mounts.

```text
FS Type = ext4, xfs, btrfs
```

### Drive Type {#b-options-drivetype}

Key: `drivetype` · Type: string list

On Windows: only back up drives of these types (fixed, removable, remote, cdrom, ramdisk).

```text
Drive Type = fixed
```

### Meta {#b-options-meta}

Key: `meta` · Type: string list

Meta information passed to plugins.

```text
Meta = "key=value"
```

### Plugin {#b-options-plugin}

Key: `plugin` · Type: string

Plugin that handles the files of this Options block.

```text
Plugin = "python3:module_name=x"
```
